correct_completion: she would have passed the exam.
full_sentence: If she had studied harder, she would have passed the exam.
acceptable_variants: she might have passed the exam.
she could have passed the exam.

options.text: she would pass the exam tomorrow.
options.why_wrong: This refers to the future, but the stem describes an unreal past situation, so the result must also be in the past.

options.text: she passes the exam every year.
options.why_wrong: This is a present habit, which does not complete the hypothetical result of the condition.

options.text: she would have passed the exam.
she has already passed the exam.
options.why_wrong: This states a real past fact, but the stem calls for an imagined result of a condition that did not happen.

explanation: The 'if' clause uses the past perfect, so the main clause needs 'would have' plus a past participle. Polish speakers may use a simple conditional form here because Polish conditionals are built with one invariable particle, so the English perfect form must be learned as a separate pattern.
